Hero.headline: Natural Code,
Hero.description: Hüma is an experimental programming language with Turkish keywords and a defined set of Turkish suffix forms. Its Rust-based interpreter is the canonical execution path; the VM and AOT support documented subsets only.

natural_syntax.title: Natural Syntax
natural_syntax.description: Code using Turkish suffixes that feel natural and improve readability.

hybrid_execution.title: Checked Execution
hybrid_execution.description: The interpreter is the canonical default path. The VM is a limited alternative that rejects unsupported syntax explicitly.

standalone_compilation.title: Experimental AOT
standalone_compilation.description: AOT accepts only a validated numeric subset and does not promise standalone binaries for general Hüma programs.

standard_library.title: Standard Library
standard_library.description: Built-in modules for math, file handling, statistics and more.

CTA.headline: Start Building Now
CTA.description: Join the community experimenting with, testing, and developing Hüma.
CTA.available_platforms: Buildable from source with the Rust toolchain

introduction.title: Intro & Philosophy
introduction.description: Discover Hüma's design principles, verified scope, and current limits.
introduction.hero_title: An Experimental Language with Turkish Keywords
introduction.hero_desc: Hüma is an experimental language with a Rust implementation and Turkish-oriented syntax. Version 0.6.0 does not claim production or critical-system readiness.

cognitive_ease.title: Cognitive Ease
cognitive_ease.desc: Turkish keywords aim to improve readability for some Turkish speakers; no study currently establishes a lower error rate.

agglutination.title: Suffix System
agglutination.desc: Only defined suffix forms are accepted after an apostrophe. Sound harmony is checked for names whose pronunciation follows from spelling; the system is not a complete natural-language analyzer.

industrial.title: Explicit Limits
industrial.desc: The interpreter is tested, but the language is pre-1.0 and has neither a static type system nor a production safety guarantee.

why_huma.title: Why Hüma?
points: Rust-based interpreter with reported runtime errors
Clear separation of interpreter, limited bytecode VM, and experimental AOT
Defined possessive, plural, and case-suffix forms
Tested CPU dense-layer and Adam training prototype

syntax.title: Basic Syntax
syntax.description: Variables, data types, and Hüma's unique suffix system.
syntax.hero_desc: Hüma's syntax offers logical clarity and flexibility. In this section, we'll examine variable definition, data types, and the heart of the language: the 'Suffix System'.

variables.title: Variable Definition
variables.desc: In Hüma, everything is a value. You can define both local and global variables with the 'olsun' keyword.

suffix_system.title: Suffix System
suffix_system.desc: Hüma accepts documented Turkish suffix forms after an apostrophe. Unknown suffixes are syntax errors; this is not a complete Turkish morphology engine.

conditionals.title: Conditionals (ise / yoksa)
conditionals.desc: Control program flow with the Turkish 'ise' (if) and 'yoksa' (else) keywords.

loops.title: Loops (olduğu sürece / range)
loops.desc: Use 'olduğu sürece' for conditional loops, and 'dan ... e kadar' for numerical ranges.

postfix_calls.title: Particle and Postfix Calls
postfix_calls.desc: Hüma supports 'ile' (with) and 'yükle' (load) structures compatible with Turkish syntax.

grammar.title: Grammar & Suffix System
grammar.description: Understanding Hüma's Turkish-oriented programming syntax and runtime interaction.
grammar.hero_desc: Hüma validates a limited, documented set of suffix forms after an apostrophe during lexing. This is a programming-language syntax rule, not a complete Turkish grammar model.

mechanics.title: How it Works?
mechanics.desc: The lexer validates apostrophe-delimited suffixes against the supported forms and emits the root token. The interpreter is the default path; the VM accepts only its documented subset.

suffixes.title: Standard Suffixes
suffixes.desc: The forms below are supported as syntax delimiters. Sound harmony is checked when pronunciation follows from spelling; the programmer remains responsible for choosing a suffix with the intended sentence-level meaning.

accusative.name: Accusative (-i, -ı)
accusative.usage: Used for printing or sending objects to functions.

dative.name: Dative (-e, -a)
dative.usage: Used for adding items to collections or navigating.

ablative.name: Ablative (-den, -dan)
ablative.usage: Used for removing items or defining ranges.

genitive.name: Genitive (-nin, -ın)
genitive.usage: Used for accessing object properties or methods. The trailing possessive suffix (hızı'ı) is now optional.

possessive.name: Possessive Suffixes
possessive.usage: Used to express object properties more naturally.

plural.name: Plural Suffixes
plural.usage: Used when operating on lists or multiple objects.

equality.name: Equality Case (-ce)
equality.usage: Used to add meaning of perspective or style.

best_practices.title: Best Practices
best_practices.desc: Genitive suffixes are structural for property access; most other suffixes are readability delimiters. Hüma does not automatically validate whether the selected form is natural Turkish.

cli.title: CLI Reference
cli.description: Current reference for the documented Hüma command-line tools.
cli.hero_desc: Hüma follows a bilingual CLI design. You can use English or Turkish commands interchangeably.

execution.title: Execution & REPL
execution.run: huma run <target> — Run a source file or a package script.
execution.repl: huma repl — Start the interactive shell.
execution.ide: There is no desktop IDE command; VS Code language files and a basic LSP are separate tools.

compilation.title: Compilation & VM
compilation.build: huma build <file> — Compile source into a versioned, integrity-checked .hbc container.
compilation.exec: huma exec <file> — Run compiled bytecode on the VM.
compilation.aot: huma aot <file> — Compile the experimental numeric subset to machine code.

package.title: Package Management
package.init: huma init — Initialize a new project.
package.new: huma new <name> — Create a project in a new folder.
package.install: huma install — Install locally distributed dependencies from huma.json.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.update: The CLI does not replace itself without a signed release channel; building from source is the verified path.
maintenance.version: huma version — Display current version info.

functions_classes.title: Functions & Classes
functions_classes.description: Hüma functions, classes, and object structures.
functions_classes.hero_desc: Hüma supports functions, lexical closures, classes, and methods. This section documents those constructs and their current behavior.

functions.title: Functions
functions.desc: Functions are the fundamental building blocks of Hüma. You can easily manage data flow with 'alsın' and 'döndür' structures.

classes.title: Classes (Object-Oriented)
classes.desc: Classes in Hüma hold data and behavior together. Object properties are accessed with the 'kendisi' keyword.

methods.title: Methods & 'kendisi' Context
methods.desc: Inside an object method, the current object is accessed with the 'kendisi' keyword.

lists_errors.title: Data Structures & Errors
lists_errors.description: List and dictionary values with catchable runtime errors.
lists_errors.hero_desc: Lists and dictionaries hold data sets. 'dene...yakala' can handle supported runtime errors in program flow; it is not an operating-system sandbox and cannot contain a process crash caused by an invalid FFI call.

lists.title: Lists & Dictionaries
lists.desc: Hüma lists are dynamic; dictionaries store key-value pairs.

errors.title: Structural Error Handling
errors.desc: Use 'dene...yakala' (try...catch) to catch runtime errors and assign the message to a variable.

stdlib.title: Standard Library
stdlib.description: Hüma's built-in API reference and helper modules.
stdlib.hero_desc: This page presents a verified selection of core functions and Hüma helper modules included in the repository.
stdlib.import_info: Use the 'yükle' directive to include a module in your project:

modules.renkler: ANSI color outputs for current terminals.
modules.liste: List mapping, filtering, and reduction operations.
modules.dosya: File read, write, and line splitting.
modules.istatistik: Mean, variance, and standard deviation calculations.
modules.rastgele: Random number generation and list shuffling.
modules.birim_test: Unit test framework: test_et, iddia_et, test_raporu.
modules.yapay_zeka: CPU dense-layer, Adam, TF-IDF, and word-embedding prototypes.
modules.ffi: Experimental dynamic-library bridge for a limited set of C ABI signatures.

compiler.title: Compiler Internals
compiler.description: Deep-dive into the Hüma compiler pipeline: lexer, suffix system, AST, and interpreter.
compiler.hero_desc: Hüma's default executor is a tree-walking interpreter implemented in Rust. The repository does not yet publish comparative performance benchmarks.

pipeline.title: The Pipeline
pipeline.desc: Hüma source code passes through four main stages: Source Text, Lexer (Tokenizer), Parser, and Interpreter.

lexer.title: Lexer & Suffix System
lexer.desc: The Hüma lexer validates defined suffix forms after an apostrophe and emits the root token. Unknown suffixes are rejected.

ast.title: Abstract Syntax Tree (AST)
ast.desc: The parser transforms the token stream into a tree of Rust enums. Each node represents a language construct: statements, expressions, and blocks.

build.title: Build from Source
build.desc: Building the Hüma compiler requires stable Rust 1.92 or newer.

changelog.title: Changelog
changelog.description: Official update history of the Hüma language and toolchain.
changelog.hero_desc: This page displays only the current release note that can be verified from repository tests and source code.

changes: Parser and runtime failures are reported as structured errors instead of being silently ignored.
Interpreter short-circuit logic, list assignment, loop control, and dene/yakala behavior are covered by regression tests.
The VM rejects unsupported syntax; AOT accepts only its validated numeric subset.
The CPU dense-layer and Adam training path is tested end-to-end with real weight updates.
Unsubstantiated capability and performance claims were removed and current limitations documented.

getting_started.title: Getting Started
getting_started.description: Build Hüma from source and run your first verifiable program.
getting_started.hero_desc: This guide shows how to build the experimental Hüma 0.6.0 toolchain from source and run a first program with the interpreter.

installation.title: Installation
installation.desc: The verified installation path is a source build with stable Rust 1.92 or newer. The CI matrix is configured to check Linux, macOS, and Windows builds.
installation.arch_desc: The core is implemented in Rust. The repository contains no benchmark supporting cross-architecture latency or performance guarantees.

quick_start.title: Verification & REPL
quick_start.desc: Verify your installation and start experimenting immediately in the interactive shell (REPL).

first_project.title: Your First Project
first_project.desc: Hüma's package manager creates a project skeleton containing a manifest and sample entry file.
first_project.suffix_desc: The 'huma paket yeni' command generates a 'huma.json' file and a main entry point.
